sum: Brookfield Corporation reported stronger third-quarter results on November 12, giving investors a fresh view of earnings growth, fundraising and capital deployment. The company said total distributable earnings reached 1.7 billion US dollars, up 16 percent from the year-earlier quarter. The figures covered the period ended September 30.

According to Brookfield Corporation, distributable earnings before realizations rose 14 percent per share to 1.5 billion US dollars, or 0.64 US dollars per share. Net income was 1.9 billion US dollars. The asset management business raised 25 billion US dollars during the quarter, while fee-bearing capital reached 682 billion US dollars.

Management also highlighted 54 billion US dollars of deployment and 20 billion US dollars of asset monetizations during the quarter. Realized net carried interest contributed 222 million US dollars to earnings. These figures keep fundraising, asset management fees and realizations at the center of the investment case.

On November 13, Markets Insider reported that JPMorgan analyst Kenneth Worthington lowered the price target to 64 US dollars from 65 US dollars while maintaining an Overweight rating. The move adds a more cautious near-term signal to a week dominated by Brookfield's operating update.

Brookfield stock: Q3 earnings rise as capital raising stays strong
sum: Brookfield Corporation reported strong third-quarter results on November 12, adding fresh financial detail to its growth strategy. The company raised 25 billion US dollars during the quarter and said total capital raised had reached 123 billion US dollars for the year, according to its Q3 2026 shareholder letter.

Distributable earnings per share, including realizations, increased 16 percent from the prior-year quarter. Distributable earnings before realizations rose 14 percent per share, while total consolidated net income reached 1.9 billion US dollars for the quarter.

Asset Management generated 755 million US dollars of distributable earnings and increased fee-related earnings 15 percent from a year earlier. Fee-bearing capital reached 682 billion US dollars, supported by fundraising across flagship and complementary strategies.

Wealth Solutions earnings grew 22 percent, with insurance assets approaching 200 billion US dollars. Brookfield also deployed 54 billion US dollars and monetized 20 billion US dollars during the quarter, while repurchasing 300 million US dollars of its shares since the previous results.

Management said the company is positioned to grow earnings by more than 15 percent annually, with additional potential from carried interest and capital allocation. The shareholder letter also highlights rising electricity demand, data centers, compute infrastructure and nuclear power as long-term investment themes.

Is Brookfield Stock a Buy, Sell, or Hold for 2027?
sum: Most Canadian investors are aware of Brookfield Corporation (TSX: BN) and at least a few of the other Brookfield tickers on the market (more on that in a moment). As we move into the last part of the year and toward 2027, it’s a good time to ask whether Brookfield stock is a buy, sell or hold right now.

The answer to that really depends on what investors expect. Brookfield is the type of business that can compound earnings over time, given some patience. That also means that growing dividend income isn’t high on the priority list of Brookfield.
In fact, Brookfield’s dividend yield is just 0.66%. In other words, investors are relying on earnings growth to support potential share price appreciation.
Brookfield operates across asset management, wealth solutions and operating businesses. That gives investors exposure to infrastructure, energy, real estate and private equity.

That’s where the myriad of other Brookfield tickers come into play. In addition to the broader corporation, there are also Brookfield listings for asset management, as well as infrastructure and renewable energy, among others.
That being said, owning the Brookfield Corporation listing does provide investors with exposure to those businesses.

For investors, this means that Brookfield has several ways from which it can generate earnings. Managing capital produces fees, while its operating businesses provide cash distributions. Finally, the insurance operations invest assets held against long-term obligations.

Brookfield stock linked to GBP 20 billion UK AI data center plan
sum: Brookfield Corporation is joining Drax and Radiant in a strategic partnership to develop an AI data center at Drax Power Station in northern England. Drax announced the agreement on Tuesday, November 3, 2026, saying Brookfield estimates that the full development could attract more than GBP 20 billion, including semiconductor chips.

The project is planned in stages. The first phase targets up to 100 megawatts of compute capacity and commercial operations from the first quarter of 2028. A second phase could add up to 500 megawatts between 2028 and 2031, while a third phase would pursue further capacity after 2031. Taken together, the partners are targeting a development above one gigawatt.

The announcement from Drax says the first phase would use power directly from the grid. Drax would provide land, power integration and planning expertise, while Radiant, Brookfield's UK-headquartered AI infrastructure platform, would lead design, customer engagement and commercialization. Investment capital and operating capabilities would come through a Brookfield-Qai AI infrastructure joint venture announced in 2025.

Drax Power Station has about 4 gigawatts of grid access, 2.6 gigawatts of active dispatchable generation and cooling systems. The site also sits close to the UK's fiber network, supporting the partners' case for developing large-scale computing capacity there.

The proposal is not yet a committed build. Phase one requires planning, regulatory and network approvals, an acceptable tenant, commercial agreements and final investment decisions from the partners. A planning application is being prepared, with public consultation expected to begin in November 2026. Later phases remain ambitions rather than confirmed developments.

Brookfield's AI infrastructure chief Sikander Rashid described the project as an opportunity to accelerate the company's strategy and support sovereign AI capacity in the UK. Drax CEO Will Gardiner said the development could help preserve jobs, support northern economic growth and strengthen the site's role in the country's energy system.

sum: Energy stocks are publicly traded companies that find, produce, transport, store, and distribute fuel and power. The sector encompasses oil and gas producers, pipeline operators, utilities, and renewable power generators, as well as companies that supply them.
Hundreds of public companies focus on energy. These five stand out for their financial strength and growth prospects.

Brookfield Renewable is a leading global renewable energy producer. It operates hydroelectric, solar, wind, and energy storage assets. The company sells energy under long-term fixed-rate power purchase agreements (PPAs) to electric utilities and other large power users. Brookfield has also invested in several sustainable solutions businesses, including carbon capture, biofuels, and nuclear services (Westinghouse).

The contracts enable Brookfield to generate relatively steady cash flows. It pays out a large portion of that money to investors via an attractive dividend. The company retains the balance to acquire, develop, and expand its renewable energy operations. In late July, Brookfield and its partners agreed to acquire Aypa, the largest standalone battery storage platform in North America, for $7 billion. The company and its partners also bought renewable power producer Boralex in a $9 billion deal that closed in August.

The deals are adding to Brookfield Renewable's enormous backlog of renewable energy and battery storage development projects. Combined with other growth drivers such as future acquisitions and higher power prices, Brookfield expects to increase its funds from operations (FFO) per share by more than 10% annually. It delivered 11% FFO per share growth in the third quarter of 2026 and 12% over the last 12 months. Brookfield's strong earnings growth should support dividend growth of 5% to 9% annually, making Brookfield a notable renewable energy dividend stock.

Bloom Energy (BE +3.42%) developed solid oxide fuel cell systems that provide ultra-resilient, highly scalable on-site electricity for large-scale facilities such as data centers. The company's power solutions are becoming an important option for data center developers seeking on-site power.

sum: The latest update is out from Brookfield Infrastructure ( (BIP) ).

Brookfield Infrastructure, a global owner and operator of long-life utility, transport, midstream and data assets, announced that it has received all required approvals for a corporate simplification combining Brookfield Infrastructure Partners and Brookfield Infrastructure Corporation into a single structure. Brookfield Asset Management stock: LXP deal closes at USD 5.2 billion
sum: Brookfield Asset Management and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board completed their acquisition of LXP Industrial Trust on Monday, November 2, 2026. The companies announced the closing in a Brookfield press release.

The all-cash transaction was valued at USD 5.2 billion, including net debt and preferred equity. LXP shareholders were entitled to USD 61.20 in cash per share, while LXP shares ceased trading on the New York Stock Exchange and the company became privately held.

LXP brings 107 industrial properties spanning approximately 52 million square feet across the U.S. Sunbelt and Midwest. Brookfield said the assets would be integrated into its global logistics platform, which covers more than 255 million square feet across over 850 properties in 20 countries.

Lowell Baron, chief executive of Brookfield Real Estate, said the acquisition reflects confidence in the long-term fundamentals of the U.S. industrial sector. He highlighted modern logistics assets, durable in-place cash flows, embedded rental growth and demand for large distribution facilities in markets with limited supply.

The closing expands Brookfield's real estate operating base but also places execution responsibility on the combined platform. Occupancy, leasing progress, rental growth and capital allocation will be central indicators for investors as the assets are integrated.

For Brookfield Asset Management, the transaction adds scale in a real estate segment tied to supply-chain infrastructure. The acquisition also increases the importance of asset-level performance and the ability to capture operating efficiencies across the enlarged logistics portfolio.

Westinghouse is a nuclear energy company that designs, builds, and maintains reactors and nuclear fuel for power plants worldwide.
Its history goes back to 1886, when inventor George Westinghouse founded the original Westinghouse Electric Corporation, and the name has stuck through several restructurings.
The nuclear business in its current form was spun off in 1999, operates as Westinghouse Electric Company, and is jointly owned by Brookfield Renewable Partners and Cameco.

items.t: Are Options Traders Betting on a Big Move in Brookfield Asset Stock?
sum: Investors in Brookfield Asset Management Ltd. BAM need to pay close attention to the stock based on moves in the options market lately. That is because the July 17, 2026 $37.50 Call had some of the highest implied volatility of all equity options today.

Implied volatility shows how much movement the market is expecting in the future. Options with high levels of implied volatility suggest that investors in the underlying stocks are expecting a big move in one direction or the other. It could also mean there is an event coming up soon that may cause a big rally or a huge sell-off. However, implied volatility is only one piece of the puzzle when putting together an options trading strategy.

Clearly, options traders are pricing in a big move for Brookfield Asset shares, but what is the fundamental picture for the company? Currently, Brookfield Asset is a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) in the Financial - Miscellaneous Services industry that ranks in the Top 42% of our Zacks Industry Rank. Over the last 60 days, one analyst has increased the earnings estimates for the current quarter, while four have dropped their estimates. The net effect has taken our Zacks Consensus Estimate for the current quarter from 45 cents per share to 44 cents in that period.

Given the way analysts feel about Brookfield Asset right now, this huge implied volatility could mean there's a trade developing. Oftentimes, options traders look for options with high levels of implied volatility to sell premium. This is a strategy many seasoned traders use because it captures decay. At expiration, the hope for these traders is that the underlying stock does not move as much as originally expected.

sum: Artificial intelligence (AI) is an important technology. However, like the internet, it seems investors have pushed AI stocks to the point where an investment bubble has formed. The internet boom ended with the dot-com crash, and Wall Street appears increasingly concerned that the AI bubble will soon burst, too.

If you are worried about that outcome, as well, you may want to do the smart thing and focus on safer investments. A good place to look is reliable dividend stocks like Dividend King Procter & Gamble (PG -1.02%), giant net lease REIT Realty Income (O -0.77%), and clean power provider Brookfield Renewable (BEP +1.63%)(BEPC +1.50%). Here's a quick look at each one.

Procter & Gamble is one of the world's largest consumer staples companies. It makes products like toothpaste, toilet paper, and cleaning products. Consumers continue buying these items no matter what is happening with the economy or the stock market. It is a very reliable business that can stand toe-to-toe with any competitor in terms of its brands, distribution, marketing, and innovation.

The real proof of that is found in this Dividend King's streak of 69 annual dividend increases. You can't build a record like that by accident. Add in an attractive 2.9% dividend yield, and this is a great alternative for investors worried about the increasing volatility of AI stocks.

Realty Income is a net lease real estate investment trust (REIT). Net leases require tenants to pay most property-level operating costs. It is a relatively low-risk investment approach in the REIT sector, and many companies use the net lease model. However, Realty Income is the largest, with a portfolio of over 15,500 properties spread across the United States and Europe.

The company's scale and investment-grade-rated balance sheet give it an advantage in accessing capital markets. A lower cost of capital allows Realty Income to compete aggressively for properties. But there's an even more interesting data point to consider. Even during the Great Recession, Realty Income's occupancy didn't fall below 96%.

If the AI bubble does burst, taking the economy with it as the dot-com bubble did, Realty Income's strong operating history suggests you'll be able to count on its dividends continuing without interruption.

sum: Increased uncertainty about the equity and credit markets tied to fiscal, tariff, and monetary policies and economic growth and increased concerns about the private credit market have sent the stocks of many alternative asset managers sharply lower.

- The private-credit-heavy alternative asset managers—Apollo Global Management APO (86% of fee-earning assets and 72% of base fees), Ares Management ARES (66% and 65%), Blue Owl OWL (53% and 61%), and KKR KKR (48% and 30%)—have been among the hardest hit. Apollo and Blackstone BX are down roughly 12% so far in 2026, Ares has lost 15%, KKR is down just shy of 16%, and Blue Owl is down nearly 18%.

- While not immune to the real and perceived headwinds in the markets, Blackstone, with its more balanced product portfolio (just 34% of fee-earning assets and 25% of base fees come from its credit and insurance segment), has seen its shares decline 12% since the start of the year—no doubt because it is the industry leader and has tended to trade at the highest multiple in the group.

- Meanwhile, Brookfield Asset Management BAM, which benefits from a heavy bent toward real estate/real assets, and Carlyle Group CG, which was coming off a couple of years of weaker performance, have been affected the least. Brookfield is up 1.0% and Carlyle is down 2.4% so far in 2026.

In September 2025, investors started to fret after both Tricolor (a subprime auto lender) and First Brands (an auto parts supplier) collapsed due to unmaintainable debt-fueled expansions, opaque off-balance-sheet financing, and outright fraud allegations. While all the finger-pointing was aimed at private credit, which has become the main lender to riskier borrowers in the aftermath of the global financial crisis, these weren’t really private credit stories.

The bulk of First Brands’ term loan debt originated in the broadly syndicated loan market. items.t: Is Brookfield Asset Management Ltd. (BAM) A Good Stock To Buy?
sum: We came across a bullish thesis on Brookfield Asset Management Ltd. on Roche Capital's Substack by Pedro Ortiz. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on BAM. Brookfield Asset Management Ltd.'s share was trading at $46.61 as of March 4th. BAM's trailing and forward P/E were 31.01 and 26.25 respectively according to Yahoo Finance.

Brookfield Asset Management Ltd. is a private equity firm specializing in acquisitions and growth capital investments. BAM delivered a record performance in FY2025, highlighting the scalability of its asset-light alternative asset management model.

The company ended the year with $603 billion in fee-bearing capital, up 12% year over year, while total assets under management reached $1.2 trillion. Fee-related earnings (FRE) increased 22% to $3 billion, supported by strong operating leverage and a 58% margin, while distributable earnings (DE) grew 14% to $2.7 billion.

Importantly, recurring fee income now exceeds total DE, indicating that BAM's current earnings are fully supported by stable management fees without relying on carried interest or investment gains. Operational momentum remained strong as the firm raised $112 billion of capital, deployed $65.6 billion, and monetized $50.1 billion for clients, demonstrating the strength of its fundraising platform and capital recycling strategy.

The firm's capital base remains highly durable, with roughly 87% of fee-bearing capital tied to long-term or perpetual structures across infrastructure, renewables, real estate, private equity, and credit. Credit is now the largest vertical with $280 billion in fee-bearing capital, supported by strategic moves such as acquiring the remaining stake in Oaktree Capital Management and purchasing a majority interest in Angel Oak Capital Advisors, strengthening BAM's position in alternative credit.

Infrastructure, renewable transition assets, and real estate platforms also continued to expand through consistent fundraising, asset deployment, and selective monetizations at attractive valuations. The balance sheet remains conservative with low leverage, ample liquidity, and long-dated debt maturities, allowing the company to maintain an investment-grade profile while returning capital to shareholders.

sum: Buying a stock for its dividend yield is a fair strategy amongst income-seeking investors. Of course, it requires doing the necessary work in order to determine if this dividend is sustainable and reliable. Ideally, the stock that we buy for yield is also experiencing dividend growth, with a reasonable expectation that this growth will continue.
In this article, I'll look into Brookfield Renewable Partners (TSX:BEP.UN), which is currently yielding a very generous 4.89%. Should you consider buying it for this dividend yield?

Brookfield is one of the world's largest publicly traded entities for renewable power and decarbonization solutions. With its hand in a diversified set of renewable energy forms, Brookfield is well-positioned to supply the world with its renewable energy needs. From onshore wind, to hydro, nuclear, solar, and battery solutions, Brookfield benefits from its scale and differentiated access to capital. This means that Brookfield can get its hands on cash relatively easily when opportunities arise.
The fact is that rising energy demand is driving the need for rapid additions of renewable capacity, baseload power, and battery storage. Brookfield can deliver across all markets at scale.

As I mentioned in my introduction, Brookfield Renewable stock is yielding approximately 4.9% at this time. Digging a little deeper, we can see that this yield is backed by a strong balance sheet, strong cash flow generation, and of course, positive industry fundamentals.

This is reflected in the fact that Brookfield instituted a 5% dividend increase in the fourth quarter of 2025. And this was not the first time that Brookfield grew its dividend so much. In fact, the partnership has 15 consecutive years of annual dividend growth of at least 5% under its belt.

As you can see from the stock price graph above, Brookfield Renewable's stock price has a lacklustre performance in recent years. But the last few years have seen a marked increase in energy demand. As the world attempts to satisfy its energy needs, Brookfield Renewable will increasingly be a beneficiary.

Is This Under-the-Radar Infrastructure Stock the Best Way to Play AI Without Buying Chips?
sum: Artificial intelligence (AI) is today's headline-grabbing technology advance. Companies are racing against each other to not only develop the best AI, but to build the infrastructure needed to support it. If you are a long-term investor, however, you don't have to focus on the AI chipmakers. There is a far more foundational need that AI can't live without and Brookfield Renewable (NYSE: BEP) (BEPC -3.39%) is happily prepared to provide it.

When you look past what artificial intelligence can do, which is truly incredible, you see that it is just a fancy computer program. Computer programs have to run on computers, which is why companies like Nvidia are all the rage on Wall Street. Nvidia makes high-powered computer chips that are capable of running AI programs.

Those chips, however, must reside in computers. Those computers have to live in buildings. So there are other ways to play the AI build-out. In fact, that's been a construction boom in the data center space. One of the limiting factors with data centers, however, is reliable electricity. You can build as many data centers as you want, but if there isn't enough electricity to power them, they are useless.

What's interesting here is that there is a risk of overbuilding in the data center property niche. Overbuilding the infrastructure that supported the internet at the turn of the century was a big problem. However, it helped usher in the widespread adoption of the internet because the overbuilding resulted in lower prices for things like fiber optic connections.

If there is overbuilding in AI, which seems highly likely given past technology booms, it is likely that the AI assets built will remain active. If history is any guide, the costs associated with using AI will fall as supply outstrips demand. The electricity needed would remain the same, if not increase, as adoption of AI spreads, thanks to falling costs.

Brookfield Renewable has already signed deals with Microsoft and Alphabet's Google to supply the clean energy that will support their AI infrastructure build-outs. While any electricity can power AI, clean and renewable energy is an increasingly important part of the global power system.
